clue.text: Bound to score in this game

parts.note: to bound is to leap or hop
to scotch is to cut or score a line, as in the lines chalked for the game

explanation.surface: A rule that you are obliged to keep score in some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but Bound is a jump and 'to' just joins it to the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground game of hopping between chalked squares is the one meant by 'this game'.

clue.text: Spirited Dutch painter?

parts.note: Pieter de ... was a Dutch painter, and his name is also slang for strong liquor, so the painter is 'spirited'

explanation.surface: A lively artist from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirits here are alcoholic drinks: the painter's surname doubles as a slang word for cheap whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for illicit or cheap spirits, sharing its spelling with the surname of a Dutch Golden Age painter.

clue.text: Coppers must accept an imposed punishment

indicators.note: something that must accept another word takes it inside itself

parts.note: copper coins are pennies, so coppers are pence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police officers have to put up with a penalty handed down to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but here it means small change.
explanation.definitionFit: A penance is a punishment undertaken or imposed to atone for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Make cracks on passing fashion

definitions.meaning: to cover a glaze or surface with a network of fine cracks

explanation.surface: Joking about a trend that will not last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make cracks on' reads as telling jokes about something, but it is the potter's sense of fine surface cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A fad is a passing fashion, and in pottery the verb means to develop fine surface cracks.

clue.text: Is in danger of falling for accountants?

definitions.meaning: people who tot up figures, jokingly

explanation.surface: Someone at risk of being smitten by bookkeepers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling for' looks like infatuation; the clue splits there, and accountants are whimsically those who tot up sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Wobbles unsteadily as if about to topple; also, punningly, people who tot up columns of numbers.

clue.text: Work of a forger, bent but possibly lucky

definitions.text: Work of a forger, bent but possibly lucky

parts.words: Work of a forger, bent but possibly lucky
parts.note: a smith at a forge makes this, it is curved, and it is a traditional good-luck charm

explanation.surface: A crooked counterfeiter's product that might still bring fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forger' and 'bent' suggest a crook, but the forger works at a forge and bent means U-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Blacksmiths forge this curved iron for a hoof, and one hung over a door is a lucky charm.

clue.text: Indicate a suitable victim

definitions.meaning: to show or point out, as by a sign
a target or dupe for a con artist

explanation.surface: Pointing out somebody ripe to be swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal or show is one sense; another is slang for a con man's easy target or dupe.

clue.text: Can come to play with model construction set

indicators.note: letters played with are juggled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to come over and tinker with a model-building kit.
explanation.walkthrough: MECCANO is a long-running British construction toy of metal strips, nuts and bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand-name toy kit of perforated metal strips and bolts for building models.

clue.text: What MPs do about now

parts.note: re means concerning or about
the present is now

explanation.surface: Asking what members of Parliament are currently up to.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Parliament act for their constituents, speaking on their behalf in the House.

clue.text: Dejected when name is not top of the bill?

definitions.text: when name is not top of the bill?
definitions.meaning: an actor billed further down the cast list

explanation.surface: An actor feeling low at not being the headline name.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as 'down' the 'cast' list.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-spirited and gloomy; whimsically, placed lower in a show's listing of performers.

clue.text: Prescription for success in the kitchen

definitions.text: Prescription for success in the kitchen

parts.words: Prescription for success in the kitchen
parts.note: a set of cooking instructions, also an old word for a doctor's prescription

explanation.surface: A formula for doing well as a cook.
explanation.walkthrough: The word once meant a medical prescription, the origin of the symbol Rx.
explanation.definitionFit: Written cooking instructions are a formula for a dish turning out well.

clue.text: Church is about to suspend innovation

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is about, that is surrounding, the other piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to hang is to suspend

explanation.surface: The Church is on the verge of halting a new development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about to' reads as 'is on the point of'; 'is about' means surrounds, and 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Innovation means introducing something new, which is a change from what went before.

clue.text: Eve's late, perhaps, but gives a lift

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Eve is running behind, but offers someone a ride anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives a lift' suggests a car ride, but here it means raises.
explanation.definitionFit: Raises or lifts up, literally or in spirits.

clue.text: Master switch for the current

indicators.note: switching the letters swaps their order around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An electrician's main switch controlling the electric current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master switch' reads as one electrical part; switch is the anagram signal and the current is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowing body of water such as a brook is a current.

clue.text: Allowance made to new cleaner

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: new signals the letters made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Extra concessions granted to a recently hired cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is only a link; 'Allowance' means forbearance, not money paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Making allowance for something means showing forbearance, or a permitted margin of variation.

clue.text: When to make me smile at cook?

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking when a chef might make me grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like a noun for the chef, but it is the verb meaning rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Times at which meals are eaten answer the question of when to eat.

clue.text: No chores undone in this vessel

indicators.note: chores undone are taken apart and put together again differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nobody does any housework aboard this boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undone' reads as tasks left unfinished, but it unpicks the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing ship with two or more masts, rigged fore-and-aft.

clue.text: Best clothes in tatters after having left to wander around

indicators.note: after places the tatters piece behind the rest
the word for roaming goes around the abbreviation for left

parts.note: to gad is to wander about
rags are tatters, torn clothing

explanation.surface: Someone's finest outfit is ragged after they have wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in tatters' looks like an anagram cue; 'in' only links and tatters means rags.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrase for someone's smartest outfit, worn for a special occasion.

clue.text: Two thousand and one in fees? They're not real

indicators.note: the numerals go in the word for fees

parts.note: dues are fees
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two thousand is MM
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Fees for the year 2001, which are mere fakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two thousand and one' looks like a year; it is MMI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop mannequins and imitations are dummies, copies rather than the genuine article.

clue.text: Weapon of no use at the front?

definitions.text: Weapon of no use at the front?

parts.words: Weapon of no use at the front?
parts.note: a weapon worn at one's flank, which by its name is not at the front

explanation.surface: An arm that is useless for soldiers on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the front' suggests the battlefront, but the joke is that this weapon is worn at the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol or sword carried at the hip is named for hanging at a soldier's flank.

clue.text: Former name to cause a stir

parts.note: ex means former
to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: Someone once famous trying to stir things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse or agitate people is to stir them up.

clue.text: A note added willingly

parts.note: an addition to a testament, so a note added to a will

explanation.surface: Someone happily jotting an extra memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willingly' sounds like readily, but means to a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplement amending a testament, added to the will after it was made.

clue.text: Made about a thousand to be burned

indicators.note: the word for made goes about, around, the numeral

parts.note: to have made something is to have created it
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Earned around a thousand, only to see it go up in smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced to ashes by fire, as a body at a crematorium.

clue.text: One habitually taking things did wrong in law

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit in the word for a law

parts.note: an act is a law passed by Parliament

indicators.note: done wrong, the letters come out in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who regularly steals has broken the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did wrong in law' reads as breaking the law; 'wrong' is the anagram cue and law is a statute.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependent on a drug habitually takes it.

clue.text: Athenian garret

explanation.surface: An attic room in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: A room just under the roof; also the adjective for Attica, the region around Athens.

clue.text: How one comes to confess

parts.note: to come ... is to own up, so this word is the manner of coming

explanation.surface: Asking how a person ends up admitting the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'come clean' means confess.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of coming clean, meaning owning up fully and honestly.

clue.text: Trendy company needing support?

parts.note: in means fashionable
a firm is a company

explanation.surface: A fashionable business in need of backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' suggests investment, but means a walking stick or a helping arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail through age or illness, so physically in need of help.

clue.text: Joins members of the embassy staff

explanation.surface: Someone joining the diplomatic staff abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastens or connects things; also diplomats with a special role at an embassy.

clue.text: Lockers A to G, perhaps

definitions.meaning: things that lock, here what turns in a lock
musical ... are named by the letters A to G

explanation.surface: Lockers numbered A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices for turning locks; also musical tonalities, named by letters from A to G.

clue.text: Monocle is readjusted half a stop

indicators.note: a readjusted thing is set up again differently, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An eyeglass being readjusted, which halts the wearer briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' is punctuation: a full stop is a period, and this mark is a half-way pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark of two dots, a pause midway between a comma and a full stop.
